about.title: Anderson Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Anderson is a small city, and when someone dies here, the loss is felt well beyond one household. In 2025, public records show 26 injury collisions in Anderson, 40 people hurt, and one traffic death. Fatal crashes and other preventable deaths on Route 273, Interstate 5, Deschutes Road, or North Street may give rise to a civil wrongful death claim in California. The law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring that claim first, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in some situations. There is a two-year deadline from the date of death, and it can be much shorter if a public agency is involved. Losses that can be recovered include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We handle these claims on a contingency basis, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children. Our team can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The two-year clock starts on the date of death, and claims against a city, county, or state agency can require notice far sooner. We act quickly to protect your family's ability to proceed.

items.title: The full picture of your loss
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. We work on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Our loved one was killed in a crash on Route 273 in Anderson. Is a wrongful death claim different from the criminal case?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family, separate from any charges the Shasta County District Attorney may pursue. The civil case focuses on your losses rather than punishment, and it can move forward whether or not a criminal case is filed or how it turns out.

items.question: How long do we have to file in California?
items.answer: Generally two years from the date of death. If a government entity may share fault, such as a road maintained by Caltrans, the county, or the City of Anderson, a formal claim must usually be presented within months, not years. Speaking with our team soon helps keep every option open.

items.question: What does it cost to contact us?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle wrongful death cases on a contingency basis. That means no fee unless there is a recovery, and you can decide at your own pace whether to move forward.
